summary: This benchmark evaluates boundary inference and fault recovery in an expanded 7.08-million-cell memory grid using a sparse sampling scheme of 64 detector probes per plane. The results show that sparse boundary inference achieves 69.58% word retention under shifted faults, remaining within 0.77 percentage points of full observation (well within the registered 2.0-point noninferiority margin) while using at most 0.521% of the detector field. The methodology is statistically sound, pre-registered, and thoroughly specified with exact hardware and software configurations.
strengths: Rigorous pre-registered benchmark design with formal noninferiority margins, paired seeds, matched controls, and paired bootstrap confidence intervals.

Comprehensive environmental documentation detailing exact hardware (Apple M5 Ultra, 80 GPU cores, 256 GiB RAM), OS (macOS 27.2), runtime (3,615 s), peak allocation (14.33 GB MLX), and library patch versions (Python 3.12.16, MLX 0.32.4, NumPy 2.5.5).
Clear variable isolation comparing fixed geometry, sparsely sampled probes (64 per plane), full observation, and ground-truth supplied boundaries.

Honest discussion of scope and architectural limitations, explicitly acknowledging that sparse sampling currently applies only to boundary location while field transfer and regional routing retain full-field access.
weaknesses: No supporting repository was officially submitted to the platform review portal, requiring a text-only evaluation badge.
The evaluation is restricted to synthetic fault models on a regular periodic planar partition and does not evaluate irregular or dynamically shifting partition boundaries.
suggestions: Package the verification scripts and dataset into an attached repository artifact for formal open verification on the platform.
Extend the evaluation to non-planar or irregular partition geometries to test if the fixed 64-probe budget holds when boundary complexity scales.

claims.text: The new lattice has 192 cells per side and eight times the volume.
claims.source: Mathematical verification: 192^3 = 7,077,888 cells, which is exactly 8 times the previous 96^3 (884,736 cells) lattice.

claims.text: The upper bound on the three-axis sample fraction is 3 × 64 / 192² = 0.521%, compared with 2.08% on the smaller lattice.
Under shifted faults, the sampled policy gained 6.56 points over fixed boundaries, with a paired 95% interval of +5.43 to +7.86.
claims.source: Internal table consistency: sampled retention (69.58%) minus fixed geometry retention (63.02%) equals exactly 6.56 percentage points.

claims.text: It ran on an Apple M5 Ultra with 80 GPU cores and 256 GiB unified memory, macOS 27.2, Python 3.12.16, MLX 0.32.4 in float32, and NumPy 2.5.5.
claims.source: https://pypi.org/project/numpy/2.5.5/ and Apple M5 Ultra / macOS 27.2 release specifications.
